title: Residue reduction and lifting a simultaneous good section
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring with exactly one maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, put $k=R/\mathfrak m$, and let $\rho:R\to k$ be the quotient map. For $t\geq0$ let $R^{\oplus t}$ and $k^{\oplus t}$ denote the coordinate modules [def-weil-pbc-free-module], and let $\rho_t:R^{\oplus t}\to k^{\oplus t}$ act coordinatewise. Given integers $m,n\geq0$ and $R$-linear maps $\alpha,\beta:R^{\oplus n}\to R^{\oplus m}$, write $a,b:k^{\oplus n}\to k^{\oplus m}$ for their coefficientwise reductions in the standard bases. Then $k$ is a field [def-weil-field], $\rho$ is a local homomorphism (the inverse image of the unique maximal ideal of $k$ is $\mathfrak m$), and surjectivity of $\alpha$ or $\beta$ implies surjectivity of $a$ or $b$, respectively. For every $k$-linear map $q:k^{\oplus m}\to k^{\oplus n}$ there exists an $R$-linear map $s:R^{\oplus m}\to R^{\oplus n}$ with $\rho_n\circ s=q\circ\rho_m$. More precisely, any choices $v_j\in R^{\oplus n}$ with $\rho_n(v_j)=q(e_j)$, for the standard vectors $e_j$ of $k^{\oplus m}$, give such a map by $s((r_j))=\sum_jr_jv_j$. Under the scalar-extension identifications $R^{\oplus t}\otimes_R k\simeq k^{\oplus t}$ given by $(r_i)\otimes c\mapsto(\rho(r_i)c)$, with inverse $(c_i)\mapsto\sum_i e_i\otimes c_i$ [def-weil-module-base-change], the scalar extensions of $\alpha\circ s$ and $\beta\circ s$ are $a\circ q$ and $b\circ q$. If $a\circ q$ and $b\circ q$ are linear isomorphisms, then every such lift $s$ has both $\alpha\circ s$ and $\beta\circ s$ linear isomorphisms over $R$, and $s$ is injective. In that case put $U=\operatorname{im}(s)\subseteq R^{\oplus n}$. The induced map $s:R^{\oplus m}\to U$ is a linear isomorphism, both restrictions $\alpha|_U$ and $\beta|_U$ are linear isomorphisms onto $R^{\oplus m}$, and $R^{\oplus n}=\ker(\alpha)\oplus U=\ker(\beta)\oplus U$. For $\gamma\in\{\alpha,\beta\}$ the projection of $x\in R^{\oplus n}$ to $U$ in this decomposition is $(\gamma|_U)^{-1}(\gamma(x))$.

proof.text: For any $R$-linear $f:R^{\oplus u}\to R^{\oplus v}$, write $f(e_j)=\sum_i f_{ij}e_i$ using the coordinate bases [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. Then $\rho_v(f(x))_i=\sum_j\rho(f_{ij})\rho(x_j)$, so coefficient reduction $\bar f$ satisfies $\rho_v f=\bar f\rho_u$. If $f$ is surjective, lift $y\in k^{\oplus v}$ to $z\in R^{\oplus v}$, choose $x$ with $f(x)=z$, and obtain $\bar f(\rho_u x)=y$. Apply this to $\alpha$ and $\beta$ separately.

proof.text: For each standard vector $e_j\in k^{\oplus m}$, surjectivity of $\rho_n$ provides $v_j\in R^{\oplus n}$ with $\rho_n(v_j)=q(e_j)$. Given any such choices, set $s((r_j))=\sum_j r_jv_j$. The finite sum is $R$-linear and $\rho_n s((r_j))=\sum_j\rho(r_j)q(e_j)=q(\rho_m((r_j)))$. The basis property [def-weil-pbc-free-module] justifies the formula on every vector, and proves the required lift for arbitrary choices.

proof.text: Define $T_t:R^{\oplus t}\otimes_R k\to k^{\oplus t}$ by $T_t(r\otimes c)=(\rho(r_i)c)_i$. The formula is additive in each argument and balanced, since $\rho(ar_i)c=\rho(r_i)(\rho(a)c)$; it therefore defines a map on the tensor product [def-weil-module-base-change]. It is $k$-linear. Define $J_t((c_i))=\sum_i e_i\otimes c_i$, also $k$-linear. Directly $T_tJ_t=1$, while on a pure tensor $J_tT_t(r\otimes c)=\sum_i e_i\otimes\rho(r_i)c=\sum_i r_ie_i\otimes c=r\otimes c$ by balancing. Pure tensors generate the tensor product, so $J_tT_t=1$. These are exactly the identifications in the statement.

source.place: Tag 0FJK, lemma-homotopic-surjections, final paragraph: explicit expansion of the omitted residue-field lift.

proof.text: For $f:R^{\oplus u}\to R^{\oplus v}$ and its coefficient reduction $\bar f$, the scalar-extension formula [def-weil-module-base-change] gives, on each pure tensor, $T_v((f\otimes_R k)(r\otimes c))=\rho_v(f(r))c=\bar f(\rho_u(r)c)=\bar f(T_u(r\otimes c))$. Thus $T_v(f\otimes_R k)T_u^{-1}=\bar f$. Using $\rho_n s=q\rho_m$ and $\rho_m\gamma=\bar\gamma\rho_n$ for $\gamma=\alpha,\beta$ identifies the reduction of $\gamma s$ with $\bar\gamma q$: both agree after precomposition with the surjection $\rho_m$. Hence the two scalar extensions are $aq$ and $bq$ as claimed.

source.place: Tag 0FJK, lemma-homotopic-surjections, final paragraph: explicit expansion of the omitted residue-field lift.

proof.text: Assume $aq$ and $bq$ are isomorphisms. For each $\gamma\in\{\alpha,\beta\}$ apply [lem-sc-local-free-base-change-reflects-iso] to the local homomorphism $\rho:R\to k$ and the map $\gamma s:R^{\oplus m}\to R^{\oplus m}$. Both rings are commutative local rings by step 1; source and target have finite coordinate bases, and step 5 identifies scalar extension with the assumed isomorphism. The cited theorem therefore makes both $\alpha s$ and $\beta s$ isomorphisms over $R$. This applies to every chosen lift, because only its reduction identity was used.

source.place: Tag 0FJK, lemma-homotopic-surjections, final paragraph: explicit expansion of the omitted residue-field lift.

proof.text: If $s(y)=0$, then $(\alpha s)(y)=0$, so $y=0$. Thus $s$ is injective and its corestriction $\widetilde s:R^{\oplus m}\to U=\operatorname{im}(s)$ is bijective; its inverse is linear, since the unique preimages of sums and scalar multiples are sums and scalar multiples of preimages. For either $\gamma$, the restriction $\gamma|_U=(\gamma s)\widetilde s^{-1}$ is an isomorphism with inverse $\widetilde s(\gamma s)^{-1}$. This proves all the image and restriction assertions.

source.place: Tag 0FJK, lemma-homotopic-surjections, final paragraph: explicit expansion of the omitted residue-field lift.

proof.text: For either $\gamma$, put $p_\gamma(x)=(\gamma|_U)^{-1}(\gamma(x))\in U$. Then $\gamma(x-p_\gamma(x))=0$, so $x=(x-p_\gamma(x))+p_\gamma(x)$ lies in $\ker\gamma+U$. If $u\in U\cap\ker\gamma$, injectivity of $\gamma|_U$ gives $u=0$. Consequently this sum is direct, and its $U$-projection is exactly $p_\gamma$. Applying the calculation to $\alpha$ and $\beta$ proves both decompositions and both projection formulas, including empty coordinate modules.
